tier_reason: Upgraded from D to C on lineage. libQD3 has no benchmark of its own, but its repo carries first-party QD timings: docs/qd.tex has the original QD authors' per-operation table against Bailey's MPFUN (CPUs, compilers and flags stated; the QD timer tests/qd_timer.cpp is public, the MPFUN harness is not). The same author's MPLAPACK manual (section 9) has upstream-QD vs MPFR/GMP Rgemm peaks (Ryzen 3970X, GCC 9.3.0, flags unstated, unequal precision). Neither measures libQD3's current code, so the tier cannot go above C.

corrections.baseline: MPFR (the MPLAPACK manual's Rgemm numbers for upstream QD against MPFR and GMP at their 512-bit default); libQD3's own docs/qd.tex also carries the original QD paper's per-operation timing table against Bailey's MPFUN
corrections.claimed_speedup: None for libQD3 itself. Lineage numbers: (1) MPLAPACK user manual (doc/manual/manual.pdf on master, titled 'MPLAPACK version 1.0.0 user manual', section 9 Benchmarks, upstream QD rather than libQD3): peak Rgemm, reference versions quad-double 33 MFlops, GMP 19 MFlops, MPFR 11 MFlops; OpenMP versions quad-double 1.3 GFlops, GMP 693 MFlops, MPFR 390 MFlops (about 3.0x MPFR single-threaded and 3.3x with OpenMP, derived from page data). (2) libQD3 docs/qd.tex timing table (original Hida/Li/Bailey QD, microseconds per operation, Pentium II 400 MHz): quad-double add 0.583, mul 1.965, sloppy mul 1.016, div 5.267 vs MPFUN add 5.729, mul 7.624, div 10.102 (about 9.8x, 3.9x and 1.9x, derived from page data); Power3 200 MHz: QD add 0.710, mul 1.131, div 6.699 vs MPFUN 4.651, 5.837, 9.180 (about 6.6x, 5.2x, 1.4x, derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: MPLAPACK run: GCC 9.3.0 inside Docker, flags not stated. docs/qd.tex table: g++ 2.95.2 -O3 -funroll-loops -finline-functions -mcpu=i686 -march=i686 (Pentium II, PowerPC 750 without the -m flags), Sun CC 5.0 -xO5 -native (UltraSparc), IBM xlC -O3 -qarch=pwr3 -qtune=pwr3 -qstrict (Power3).
corrections.hardware: MPLAPACK Rgemm run: AMD Ryzen Threadripper 3970X, 256 GB DDR4-3200 (the manual says ECC is not enabled for the Rgemm runs and 'ECC Unbuffered' for the Raxpy runs), Docker. docs/qd.tex table: Intel Pentium II 400 MHz, Sun UltraSparc 333 MHz, PowerPC 750 266 MHz, IBM Power3 200 MHz.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 2 stars, 0 forks, 158 commits on main; MPLAPACK (same author, 108 stars) uses libQD3 as its QD back end per the MPLAPACK README
corrections.caveats: Why only C: no measurement of libQD3 itself exists; both number sets cover the QD double-double/quad-double code that libQD3 inherited (the README says the fork 'keeps the original double-double and quad-double functionality'), not its new td_real, edd_real or binary32 types or the optional branch-free paths (CHANGES.1.2.0.md says those follow the Kouya/Zhang-Aiken algorithms; no timings given). The MPLAPACK manual numbers predate libQD3 (upstream QD), compare unequal precisions (quad-double about 212 bits vs MPFR and GMP at 512 bits), run through MPLAPACK's C++ wrappers (in the Raxpy section the author suspects the MPFR C++ binding makes needless copies, since MPFR ran at half of GMP's speed), and are not peer reviewed; the manual opened is titled version 1.0.0 (search results title arXiv 2109.13406 'MPLAPACK version 2.0.1 user manual'; arXiv is blocked here and was not opened). The docs/qd.tex table is from about 2000 (Pentium II, g++ 2.95.2), compares against MPFUN rather than MPFR, and the MPFUN harness is not in the repo; tests/qd_timer.cpp times QD only. docs/td.tex gives flop counts, not timings: TD add 41 flops vs QD 84, TD mul 116/206 (FMA/no FMA) vs QD 182/332, and states FMA gives about 1.8x for multiplication and 1.6x for division (the 2.7x figure is DD's 24/9 ratio, derived from page data). Licensing: LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause; COPYING (LBNL notice) asks commercial users to contact LBNL's Technology Transfer Department, and the td.tex abstract says 'BSD 2-clause', which does not match LICENSE. Related lineage evidence not opened (arXiv blocked): Kouya, arXiv 1510.08642, a table titled 'Computational times of QD and MPFR/GMP (212 bits) matrix multiplication' (equal precision, upstream QD); Kouya, arXiv 2603.14926 (ICCSA 2026 workshops), branch-free TD/QD with SIMD; a search summary says TD 1.2-1.5x and QD 1.4-2.0x 'compared to MPFR' for matrix multiplication, unverified and possibly branch-free vs conventional.

notes: Tier raised D to C because libQD3's own docs/qd.tex carries QD vs MPFUN timings and the MPLAPACK manual numbers check out exactly (33/19/11 MFlops, 1.3 GFlops/693/390 MFlops). Every number covers inherited upstream QD code rather than libQD3's current build, so drop it back to D if the catalog wants project-specific measurements only. Metadata checked: BSD-3-Clause, fork of BL-highprecision/QD, last commit 2026-09-19, active.

tier_reason: The README gives first-party wall-clock numbers against the CPU GMP-ECM path: the RTX 4080 Pollard's rho takes about 8.7 s for a 16-digit factor vs about 2 s for CPU ECM. Methodology is partial (Makefile flags and GPU model, no benchmark harness, CPU for the comparison not named), so the evidence is C. It shows the GPU programs are slower, and the CPU path claims no win over plain GMP-ECM.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: CPU: /usr/bin/gcc -O3 -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -funroll-loops -ftree-vectorize -ftree-slp-vectorize -fopenmp, -D_GNU_SOURCE -D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700, link -lecm -lgmp -lm -flto=32 -O3. GPU: nvcc (/usr/local/cuda-12.9, also tested with CUDA 13.2) -O3 -arch=sm_89 (sm_120 on Blackwell), OpenMPI 5.0.5 via mpicxx --showme, GMP-ECM 7.0.6 (from the Makefile and README).
corrections.caveats: Does not qualify as faster than its baseline. The README ('Performance reality') and primefactors-design.pdf both say neither GPU program is meant to beat the CPU GMP-ECM path: GPU rho is about 4x slower on a 16-digit factor (8.7 s vs 2 s, derived from page data), 'much slower' below 2^64 because of CUDA/MPI start-up cost, and impractical at 19 or more digits. The CPU program wraps GMP and libecm with its own trial division, Pollard's rho and OpenMP curve-parallel ECM scheduling, but makes no comparison against the stock ecm binary or single-threaded GMP-ECM; its 30/35/40-digit wall-clock figures (about 10.5 s, 20.6 s, 5.7 min) come from an unidentified 32-core box. The design doc's ~37 s to ~8.65 s (~4.3x) is GPU-vs-GPU tuning; three further GPU 'optimizations' were reverted as net-slower (Brent batched gcd about 2.6x slower, per-instance ILP 2-4x slower, __launch_bounds__ capping). Kept as a record so the shortcoming is documented. The README says the author used Claude Opus 5.0 for the Pollard's rho code and for testing and bug finding. The author's CGBN fork (steleman/nvidia-cgbn) was not examined.

notes: Reject (not-faster): by the author's own numbers the GPU paths are slower than CPU GMP-ECM, and the CPU path claims nothing over plain GMP-ECM. Under the keep-and-document rule, record the 'not faster' shortcoming. Metadata checked: MIT, 1 star, 0 forks, 7 commits, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-01 (active).
